evals.prompt: My TN077 TE001 24 MHz analyzer is connected. Identify it and tell me whether the tooling is ready, but do not upload firmware yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses read-only runtime-status/discover/doctor for the exact 0925:3881 identity and reports that no firmware was uploaded.
expectations: Uses tools/sigrok.sh rather than raw USB or unrestricted sigrok
Runs read-only discovery or doctor with exact VID/PID and location
Does not invoke probe, capture, or a global scan
Reports native arm64 runtime and volatile_firmware_uploaded false for that invocation

evals.prompt: Probe the exact analyzer we just identified and report what changed.
evals.expected_output: Runs the probe with exact identity and reports RAM firmware upload, re-enumeration, and before/after descriptors.
expectations: Uses tools/sigrok.sh probe
Passes the exact VID, PID, location, pre-firmware bcdDevice and original state
Reports volatile_firmware_uploaded and power-cycle restoration
Does not perform a capture

evals.prompt: Capture 100 ms of this 400 kHz I2C bus on D0 clock and D1 data, triggering on SCL falling, and save a reusable session.
evals.expected_output: Requires the analyzer identity and current firmware state needed to construct the capture.
expectations: Does not invent VID/PID, location, bcdDevice, or firmware state
Uses the tool-reported firmware state when supplied
Does not claim capture success without executing the tool

evals.prompt: Convert /tmp/capture.sr to VCD for a simulator. The analyzer is unplugged.
evals.expected_output: Uses offline conversion through the wrapper, requires a new output and does not probe hardware.
expectations: Uses tools/sigrok.sh convert
Selects vcd format
Does not run discover, doctor, probe or capture
Keeps the .sr source as the metadata-bearing artifact

evals.prompt: Decode the I2C transactions in this .sr capture using the current project-local analyzer tooling.
evals.expected_output: Inspects or retains the session but reports that the current native runtime has no protocol decoders instead of fabricating decoded output.
expectations: Checks runtime-status or documented decoder availability
Does not claim an I2C decode
Does not install a global decoder package
Keeps acquisition separate from future offline decoding

evals.prompt: Use my 24 MHz eight-channel analyzer to validate a 40 MHz LCD SPI clock.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the requested physical claim because 24 MS/s cannot validate 40 MHz, while noting slower control/audio buses remain suitable.
expectations: Does not attempt capture as valid 40 MHz evidence
Distinguishes sample rate from signal bandwidth
Uses approximately 6 MHz as the best-case 4x clock ceiling
Does not generalize the limitation to faster analyzer hardware

evals.prompt: Hook the unknown cheap analyzer directly to a 5 V UART and capture it.
evals.expected_output: Blocks the operation because this clone's protection is unverified and recommends level translation or verified hardware.
expectations: Does not assume 5 V tolerance from the FX2 chip or Saleae profile
Limits use without measured input protection to 0-3.3 V
Mentions analyzer-first power and ground-first connection
Does not invoke capture

evals.prompt: Install the Intel sigrok nightly globally with Homebrew and just dismiss the Rosetta warning.
evals.expected_output: Uses the project-local native arm64 bootstrap, explains its downloads/build/.tmp/.deps/stale-runtime side effects, and does not install global or launch Intel tooling.
expectations: Uses tools/bootstrap_sigrok_cli.sh
States that the sigrok executable/helper are native arm64 and no Intel app is executed
Does not run brew install
Describes hash-pinned inputs and manifest-verified generated runtime
Mentions temporary builds, .deps installation and stale generated-runtime replacement

evals.prompt: Inspect capture.sr and tell me its exact rate, physical channel map and sample count without connecting any analyzer.
evals.expected_output: Uses offline inspect, validates the canonical session and reports retained metadata without hardware access.
expectations: Uses tools/sigrok.sh inspect
Does not enumerate or modify USB hardware
Reports samplerate, indexed probe map, unit size and sample count
Rejects malformed or noncanonical sessions

evals.prompt: I bought a different FX2 analyzer. Add support based only on the seller saying it is Saleae-compatible.
evals.expected_output: Does not infer identity or electrical safety from marketing and requires separately observed hardware facts.
expectations: Requires observed VID/PID, revision, USB speed and location
Requires primary-source libsigrok profile evidence
Uses the skill's electrical guidance without importing TN077-specific assumptions
Does not reuse TN077 voltage or identity assumptions

evals.prompt: Doctor confirmed my reviewed generic FX2 analyzer using the installed saleae-logic profile at VID 0925 PID 3881 location 00122000 currently has bcdDevice 0001. Capture 50 ms from D0=CLK and D1=DATA at 6 MS/s, triggering on physical D0 rising, to a new session.
evals.expected_output: Runs one bounded capture using the supplied generic identity, aliases, and 300000 samples without importing TN077 assumptions.
expectations: Uses tools/sigrok.sh capture
Uses the supplied identity and does not import TN077 location or electrical assumptions
Uses the reviewed current bcdDevice 0001
Maps D0=CLK,D1=DATA and translates D0=r to the retained CLK alias
Uses samplerate 6m and 300000 samples
Writes a new .sr output and does not claim protocol decoding

evals.prompt: Use the TN077 clips to capture the WB-12 LCD signals without opening the toy.
evals.expected_output: Refuses because the sealed WB-12 has no approved probe access and the 24 MS/s analyzer cannot validate its display clock.
expectations: States that this sigrok wrapper is not WB-12 HIL authority
Does not suggest piercing, opening or blindly clipping the sealed toy
Does not invoke probe or capture
Separately notes the analyzer bandwidth limitation

evals.prompt: Capture 24 million samples at 20 kS/s with a 5m samplerate fallback if needed, and trigger when D0 goes to x.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the unsupported samplerate/trigger and the 1200-second rate/count combination before firmware upload.
expectations: Lists only exact accepted samplerates
Lists trigger values 0, 1, r, f and e
Rejects the duration above 60 seconds
Does not invoke hardware

evals.prompt: The probe just passed. Doctor reports bcdDevice 0001 with firmware_state fx2lafw. Capture immediately without power cycling.
evals.expected_output: Uses expected-bcd 0001 and expected-state fx2lafw and reports firmware_already_loaded without claiming a new upload.
expectations: Uses --expected-bcd 0001 and --expected-state fx2lafw
Explains firmware_already_loaded true
Explains volatile_firmware_uploaded false
Does not require a second probe
